components.html:
How to use Presenter

  1. 1Drop a deck. Paste, choose, or drag an HTML file anywhere on the page.
  2. 2Present. Click a Recent decks row to open it full-screen.
  3. 3Move. ← → or Space; Home/End jump; F fullscreen.
  4. 4Notes & help. N notes; ? all shortcuts; Esc closes notes, then exits.
  5. 5Zoom & pan. Use − / + in the status bar; hold Ctrl/Cmd and drag to pan while zoomed.

Keys

← →
Previous / next
F
Fullscreen
N
Notes
?
All shortcuts
Esc
Close, then exit
Ctrl + drag
Pan while zoomed

Make a deck with your LLM. Ask for one self-contained HTML file with a fixed 1920×1080 stage, one .slide per page, inline CSS/JS, and arrow-key navigation. Drop the file here.

narrative.overview: The app is a charcoal drafting table in a dark rehearsal room. Decks are storyboard frames pinned to the wall, numbered in the margin and held by tape; the only warm light is a single gold work lamp. The interface is deliberately closer to a director's cue sheet than to a dashboard: precise linework, honest materials, and handwritten marginalia only where a person would actually write a note. The system serves an Operate surface, so familiarity and keyboard speed outrank expression. The start screen is a clean, PowerPoint-like launcher: a blank 16:9 New deck tile and a Recent decks list. The storyboard world lives in the deck thumbnails, taped dialogs, Rehearse console, and the built-in tour. The presentation stage itself is pure black and carries no decoration beyond the counter, the progress rule, and the split console. The AI prompt builder and speaker-notes editor are taped authoring sheets, not a slide editor.
keyCharacteristics: Charcoal ground with a faint 32px drafting grid and a restrained gold pool of light.
A blank 16:9 New deck tile and a scannable Recent decks list; frames, ticks, and tape belong to the thumbnails and dialogs, not the launcher.
Gold is a work light, not a brand wash: primary action, focus, progress, and frame numbers.
Handwriting is marginalia only; controls, labels, and data use system UI or mono.
Flat at rest; soft depth appears only for hover, dialogs, notes, and toasts.
The New deck tile persists when decks exist; the recent list grows beside it, and the guide/tour live in the header.
The topbar stays product-only; the Utharam maker lockup and install affordance live in the app footer.
One screen defaults to Present without notes; extended displays add a private speaker window; one display uses a split Rehearse deck + console.
The AI prompt builder and library speaker-notes editor make notes explicit and optional; Rehearse splits the deck and console on one display, and the presentation mode decides whether notes are used.

rules.name: The One Work-Light Rule
rules.body: Gold is used on the primary action, focus, progress, frame numbers, and active notes cues. It never fills large surfaces or decorates inactive states; its rarity is what makes it read as light.

rules.name: The No Warm Paper Rule
rules.body: The ground is charcoal, never cream. Tape and handwriting may suggest paper, but the surface stays dark so the app and the deck never compete.

rules.name: The Handwriting-Is-Marginalia Rule
rules.body: The hand face appears only in the empty state, the notes hint, and similar annotations. It never sets a control, a label, a number, or a heading that must be scanned quickly.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Measurement Rule
rules.body: Mono is for frame numbers, dates, byte sizes, slide counters, keycaps, and field labels. It is not a costume for general body copy.

rules.name: The Soft-Depth Rule
rules.body: Shadows are soft, offset, and state-driven. Hard offset block shadows and zero-offset colored halos do not belong to this world.

dos:
Do keep the New deck tile and Recent decks list as the first view.
Do accept a file drop anywhere on the library page and show the drop overlay.
Do keep the presentation stage pure black; only the status bar and notes card may overlay the deck.
Do use the 2px gold focus ring on every real control, with 2px offset.
Do keep the hand face for marginalia and the mono face for measurements.
Do use soft, offset shadows only for state and overlays.
Do preserve the recent-row anatomy: 16:9 thumbnail, frame number, title, mono metadata, Present, mode caret, Notes, and Delete.
Do give every overlay a native dialog or labelled dialog role and restore focus on close.
Do default one display to Present without notes; offer speaker view only on an extended display.
Do treat S as speaker view: the speaker window on an extended display, the split Rehearse view on one display.
Do keep the prompt builder and notes editor taped, plain, and consistent with the add sheet; they are authoring tools, not a slide editor.
donts: Don't put a kicker or eyebrow above a heading.
Don't use gradient text, glass/blur decoration, colored side stripes, or hard offset shadows.
Don't use emoji or Unicode glyphs as icons; draw inline SVG.
Don't nest a card inside a card or turn the library into an icon + heading + text feature grid.
Don't use the hand face for controls, data, or body copy.
Don't let gold fill large surfaces or decorate inactive states.
